trust_boundaries: agentic-to-tools: tool_registry to web_search, code_execution, database_tool, api_integrations
agentic-to-data: agent_orchestrator to vector_db, document_store, user_db
sandbox: code_execution isolated from host filesystem
architecture_summary.operational_context: Agentic AI system with multi-LLM RAG pipeline, tool calling, and code execution sandbox

threat_actors.name: Adversarial User
threat_actors.motivation: Prompt injection to hijack agent behaviour, exfiltrate other users' data, or abuse tool calling
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Chat interface — crafted prompts designed to manipulate agent_orchestrator
non_capabilities: No direct API access beyond the chat UI
No access to system prompts or prompt_manager configuration
No credentials for vector_db or document_store
No ability to modify tool_registry configuration

threat_actors.name: Malicious External Content
threat_actors.motivation: Indirect prompt injection via poisoned documents ingested into vector_db or retrieved by web_search
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Content injected into indexed documents or served from web search results
non_capabilities: No direct system access — influence limited to content the agent retrieves
No access to audit_log or session_store
No ability to modify tool_registry directly

threat_actors.name: External Model Provider Compromise
threat_actors.motivation: Supply chain attack — backdoored or manipulated responses from external LLM provider
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Provider API compromise or targeted backdoor in model deployment
non_capabilities: Cannot access internal data stores directly
Cannot execute code on internal infrastructure
Influence limited to LLM response content processed by agent_orchestrator

attack_paths.entry_point: User-supplied prompt containing instruction override via chat interface
attack_paths.impact: Agent executes attacker-directed actions — data exfiltration, tool misuse, or confidentiality violation
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Prompt injection is the primary attack vector for agentic systems; agent_orchestrator processes all user input

attack_paths.entry_point: Adversarial instructions embedded in documents ingested into vector_db
attack_paths.impact: Indirect prompt injection — retrieved context contains malicious instructions agent follows
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: RAG retrieval of adversarial documents is a known attack; requires attacker-controlled document to enter corpus

attack_paths.entry_point: API key leakage from agent_orchestrator environment or logs
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized LLM inference at attacker scale, cost hijacking, potential model probe for jailbreak
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: LLM API keys frequently leaked in logs or environment variables; high-value for cost and abuse

attack_paths.entry_point: Agent instructed via AP-001 to execute attacker-controlled code in sandbox
attack_paths.impact: Sandbox escape or data exfiltration via code execution capabilities of the agent
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Code execution tools are high-value targets; sandbox escape techniques depend on isolation quality

attack_paths.entry_point: Agent directed via AP-001 to retrieve and summarise sensitive documents
attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of confidential documents via agent's summarisation and output to attacker
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Document retrieval is a primary agent function; prompt injection that redirects retrieval is straightforward

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised model weights in local_llm via supply chain or model repository
attack_paths.impact: Backdoored local model produces attacker-controlled outputs on specific trigger inputs
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires compromise of model supply chain; high sophistication but significant impact for a locally deployed LLM

attack_paths.entry_point: Session token theft from session_store via agent-mediated access or injection
attack_paths.impact: Account impersonation enabling access to other users' conversation history and documents
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Session tokens in session_store accessible to agent; injection-driven session theft is an escalation of AP-001

attack_paths.entry_point: Agent instructed via AP-001 to suppress logging of its own actions
attack_paths.impact: Agent actions during attack are not recorded; investigation and detection is impaired
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Audit log writes typically go through a separate pathway; depends on whether agent has write access to audit_log

attack_paths.entry_point: XSS or CSRF vulnerability in chat web interface
attack_paths.impact: Session hijacking or forced agent actions on behalf of victim user
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Standard web vulnerabilities apply; modern frameworks reduce likelihood but not eliminate

mitigations.control_name: Prompt injection detection and input sanitisation layer
Document ingestion scanning for embedded instructions
LLM API key rotation and secrets management
Code execution sandbox hardening with syscall filtering
Document access control — per-user scoping for agent retrieval
Model provenance verification and integrity checks for local_llm
Session token binding and short TTL
Immutable audit log — agent cannot modify its own audit trail
Content Security Policy and CSRF tokens on web_ui

findings.severity_rationale: Prompt injection without effective guardrails gives attacker full agent control; tool_registry access means real-world actions beyond conversation
No per-user document scoping means agent can retrieve any document in the store for any user via injection
Adversarial RAG documents create indirect injection channel; document ingestion without scanning makes this persistent
Code execution sandbox provides escalation path if prompt injection succeeds; sandbox escape has high impact
Session token theft is secondary to injection; partial session binding limits scope
Local LLM backdoor is low probability but high impact; model integrity verification not in place
LLM API key leakage risk mitigated by rotation; residual risk is cost hijacking, not data breach

agentic.blast_radius: User document exfiltration, external API calls to untrusted services, code execution in sandbox with potential escape, external web requests to attacker-controlled URLs
human_oversight_points: Document ingestion approval not implemented — automated
Tool call approval not implemented — agent executes autonomously
